Renovating with quotes you actually understand

You want to renovate, and the quotes are hard to compare. GRENFORD obtains them on a common basis and puts them side by side, line by line.

Have quotes compared↓Determine value after renovation ↓
ServicesValue after renovationFeesBefore & afterRenovation Memo5-Point ProcessFAQContact

Why three quotes are rarely comparable

The differences usually lie in scope, quantities and specification, not in price. In the Renovation Memo, original quotes are first compared anonymously as A, B and C.

Make them comparable

All firms price the same scope of works. What is missing, what is unclear and what costs more becomes visible line by line.

Decide personally

You meet two firms on site and decide yourself whom to commission. GRENFORD remains your point of contact until completion.

Who pays for the advice?

Not you, and not through a mark-up either.

GRENFORD is paid by the construction company you ultimately commission. Every firm already budgets for sales costs, whether for advertising, preliminary site visits or quotes that never get commissioned. GRENFORD’s fee replaces part of these and does not come on top. Four rules ensure this. Whether and whom you commission is your decision alone.

Same for everyone

The fee is fixed before the tender round and is the same for every participating firm. The comparison stays fair.

Paid from saved costs

The firms receive a finished scope of works and a client ready to decide. Canvassing, preliminary visits and speculative quotes are no longer needed.

Competition

At least three quotes on the same basis. A firm that adds a mark-up loses the comparison.

Disclosed in the memo

The amount of the fee is stated in the Renovation Memo. You commission the firm yourself; payments are made only between you and the firm.

Frequently asked questions

Do you take on site management or technical acceptance?＋

No. Construction, site management and technical acceptance are not part of the advice. GRENFORD has no authority to accept works; if needed, you commission an architect or expert for this.

Does the model suit smaller jobs?＋

For smaller jobs, a simplified memo can make sense. The right scope is clarified in the initial conversation.
